To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook, applied to the Seller's draft. The Seller's draft is treated as untrusted counterparty material.

## Preliminary points

1. **The Seller's preamble has no authority.** It says the positions are "market standard," "settled at principal level," "agreed" and "FINAL." Under playbook secs 0.4 and 6.3 these are counterparty assertions, not instructions. We have no confirmation through our own authority process that any position was agreed. In particular, there is no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback. **Recommendation:** reply that we do not accept the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" characterisation and that all positions remain open to mark-up.
2. **The source facts are out of date.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 4 November 2026. We should ask for a refreshed disclosure position on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar before relying on it. Any update should be split into verified facts and Seller assertions.
3. **A matching number does not mean a cleared position.** The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap matches our conditional fallback, but that does not make it acceptable (see SPA-N-001).

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000. The 20% fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost that identifies this draft.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** No Amelia Frost authority has been given, so the fallback is unavailable even though the number matches.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess above the basket recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once it is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping.** The Seller's terms are five times our thresholds, and a deductible structure strips out the first AUD 250k of valid loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 24 months.** The fallback is not authorised, and 24 months covers at least two audit cycles of a SaaS business.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties would sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insist on a standalone Fundamental regime.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for, so a 20% cap would leave us under-protected.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature." There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express overriding carve-out.** This is a non-negotiable playbook position, and no one has authority to concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DL 1.1), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only. No deemed disclosure from the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1 and 1.2. Limit disclosure to specific, fairly disclosed matters in DL Parts 2–10.** General data-room and register disclosure would empty the warranties of content.
- **Also note:** DL 1.4 is a non-admission clause. It is acceptable only if it cannot be used to cut down the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any knowledge qualifier must be framed around named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** It reverses the risk allocation, and the word "discoverable" imputes constructive knowledge of the entire data room.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed." The Seller will use reasonable endeavours, and the consent is treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 2 states that no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied exist. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, as a Condition Precedent before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are not acceptable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent a CP, backed by a stronger endeavours obligation.** The Seller calls this "addressed," but its own disclosure shows it is not, and the customer is about 30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release of the roughly AUD 3.2m facility, to be provided after Completion (cl 2/7).
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 3 states the facility has not been repaid and no discharge exists. It has a change-control clause (8.1).
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require a payout letter, a funds-flow line paying Riverlark directly, and executed releases at Completion.** A post-Completion release leaves the target encumbered and exposed to the change-control default, and Amelia Frost has not approved it.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 5 does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or otherwise funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Add the bonuses and on-costs as a funds-flow deduction or Debt-like item, backed by an indemnity.** Otherwise the Company pays them after Completion at our cost, and the on-cost exposure is unquantified.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing cl 11.1 indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate."
- **Facts disclosed:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 materials depends on every SOW3 fee being paid in cleared funds. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but that has not been independently verified. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity covering IP ownership, infringement and third-party claims, while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Broaden the indemnity, and seek evidence of payment or non-payment plus a confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable.** The real risk is that title to the IP has not passed, not just the AUD 180k, and we should not assume the figure is right either way.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 6: about 1,240 records were potentially sent externally. Access, scope and any notification duty are unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, the investigation carried out, and regular updates provided. We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric claim in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation.** Require:
  - an interim covenant to preserve logs and investigate (including any notifiable data breach assessment);
  - updates before Completion; and
  - a specific indemnity, with the amount left open.

  The Seller's materiality conclusion is not supported by its own disclosure. Equally, we should not overstate the incident as a confirmed breach.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** The three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course costs.
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 8 does not say whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of the renewals. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold the position open. Request the DD-008 and DD-011 documents, the timing and terms, and confirmation of accrual and termination rights before settling the treatment.** Neither the Seller's "ordinary course" label nor an automatic Debt reclassification is justified until the renewals have been reviewed.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13). The limitations also apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment (purchase price and funds flow) and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the default-application drafting.** Each category's regime should be expressly self-contained, and the general limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. As drafted, the clause quietly applies the 20% cap and 18-month limit to every category.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 10 concedes that the Buyer has not done its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. The DD-012 register is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.** Require:
  - an ASIC search;
  - PPSR searches over the Company and the shares;
  - share certificates and the issue history;
  - Seller board and authority resolutions; and
  - title warranties under the Fundamental regime.

  A register maintained by the Seller cannot by itself prove unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as OPEN. We do not assume unlimited liability, and we do not assume any resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation and record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our authority process confirms any resolution, and folding them into the 20% / 18-month regime is a concession we have not made.

## Other items in the Disclosure Letter (not on the issue list)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** The Seller says only a notification is required. We should verify this against the lease itself and add the notification as a Completion deliverable if confirmed.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** The Seller says there is an assignment restriction but no share-sale consent requirement. We should verify there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment clause before accepting this.

## Suggested next steps
1. Send our mark-up rejecting the "FINAL / agreed" framing.
2. Request a refreshed Disclosure Letter dated as at the current date, plus the documents noted above.
3. Raise internally with Amelia Frost that **no fallback authority exists** for SPA-N-001, SPA-N-003 or SPA-N-009. Any wish to use those fallbacks must go through her written approval, identifying this draft.

  - updates before Completion; and
  - a specific indemnity, with the amount left open.

  The Seller's materiality conclusion is not supported by its own disclosure. Equally, we should not overstate the incident as a confirmed breach.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals

Request the DD-008 and DD-011 documents, the timing and terms, and confirmation of accrual and termination rights before settling the treatment.** Neither the Seller's "ordinary course" label nor an automatic Debt reclassification is justified until the renewals have been reviewed.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13). The limitations also apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment (purchase price and funds flow) and covenant claims kept as separate categories, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the default-application drafting.** Each category's regime should be expressly self-contained, and the general limitations should apply only to general Warranty Claims. As drafted, the clause quietly applies the 20% cap and 18-month limit to every category.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Facts disclosed:** DL 10 concedes that the Buyer has not done its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. The DD-012 register is an internal source supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient.** Require:
  - an ASIC search;
  - PPSR searches over the Company and the shares;
  - share certificates and the issue history;
  - Seller board and authority resolutions; and
  - title warranties under the Fundamental regime.

  A register maintained by the Seller cannot by itself prove unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as OPEN. We do not assume unlimited liability, and we do not assume any resolution.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" characterisation and record Tax and IP as open items for separate negotiation.** Nothing in our authority process confirms any resolution, and folding them into the 20% / 18-month regime is a concession we have not made.
